questions.question: In a no passing zone, what can a motorcycle do?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it can be done before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the road.

questions.question: During the day, you should ride with your headlight:

options.text: On only if it is cloudy.
On only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch both feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch both feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to reach and operate the controls easily.

questions.question: You have been drinking. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can stay in your body even at this rate. Your ability to ride and make good decisions can still be affected.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. Someone drank eight drinks four hours ago. How many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active ingredient in marijuana is called THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can slow down by downshifting. Remember that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: The best lane position is the one that:

options.text: Allows you to draft off other vehicles.
Allows other motorists to see you.
Places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows other motorists to see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Only required for passengers without their own license.

questions.explanation: Oregon law requires all motorcycle operators and passengers to wear a DOT-approved helmet.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
Are not helpful because you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of normal riding. Always check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise exposure while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing is not really for protection.
No, clothing is more of a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing can reduce injury risk in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of strong material, and fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: Motorcycles must have all of the following, except:

options.text: A minimum of one headlight, but no more than three headlights.

questions.explanation: Oregon requires motorcycles to have: 1 to 3 white headlights, at least one red taillight, one white license plate light, at least one red brake light, amber turn signals (if built after 1972), a red rear reflector, at least one rearview mirror, a horn, fenders on all wheels, at least one brake, and a working exhaust system. All lights must be DOT-compliant.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to take roads that are not crowded.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if necessary. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be performed by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you will be carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough pre-ride inspection before every ride. It should take just a few minutes.

questions.question: What can help reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single best way to reduce your risk of head or neck injury in a crash.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.explanation: Only time lets your body eliminate alcohol. There is no quick way to sober up.

questions.question: The proper body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Allows you to sit far enough forward that your arms will be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
Allows you to sit as far back as possible and have to stretch when trying to reach the handle grips.
Makes you lean over the bike, requiring your arms to hold you up.
Allows for your knees to be kept far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to sit far enough forward that your arms will be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Sit far enough forward so your arms are slightly bent when you hold the handle grips. This lets you easily and comfortably reach and use the controls.

questions.question: When consumed together, the effects of alcohol and drugs:

options.text: Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is consumed alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can make riding unsafe. Some drugs become even more dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: How can you increase your chances of being seen at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position yourself in the lane so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane at all times.
Weave between lane positions to keep other drivers away.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where you position yourself in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position in the lane based on how road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. It is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to make yourself more visible. Bright clothing with reflective materials helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which of the following does not protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.
